correctness.rationale: The theorem counts each length-L binary input once. A three-component state tracks the previous digit and the separate multiplication and binomial-addition carries. Kummer counts only the latter; the explicit four-zero-bit terminal weights include all outstanding carries. This proves P_L=e1^T T^L w for all L, and exact rational matrix inversion proves F_0 and F_1. The accompanying verify.py confirms the symbolic identities by exact cancellation, plus independently compares all valuation histograms via binary digit sums for 0<=L<=15. The finite test is supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Specific exact complete distribution on a (5,2) binomial ray, including valuation-one function z(1-z^2)^2/Q^2, was not identified in examined primary sources, OEIS and published research records. Both the earlier zero-layer OEIS recurrence and a different four-state (3n,n) ray result are acknowledged. Their statements do not logically imply the present new eight-state mixed-carry result, although a general digital-enumeration framework might do so and remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The natural 2-adic divisibility distribution of binomial(5n,2n) over dyadic intervals has an exact all-level answer, not merely one new term in a table. The first nonzero shell has explicit rational GF z(1-z^2)^2/Q^2, in contrast with the zero first shell of the simpler binomial(3n,n) ray. A second digit-carry mechanism makes the case structurally different, and its full exact fibres have potential uses in arithmetic digital statistics. This is a motivated self-contained natural invariant, not a claim of a new general matrix method.
